# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 OTE | Reports to Partnerships (partner-facing applied AI architecture) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s enterprise opportunity depends on making advanced AI practical for organizations while maintaining a strong reliability and safety posture. In this context, partner architecture is a scaling function: it converts platform
capability into customer-ready delivery methods that external teams can apply consistently.

The central challenge is not simply growing partner activity. It is creating enough technical consistency that customers receive credible guidance across clouds, consultancies, technology firms, and industry contexts, without slowing the
pace of commercial expansion or forcing every deployment through a central team.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic presents itself as an AI research and safety company building systems intended to be reliable, interpretable, and steerable. Its commercial footprint brings that mission into business and developer environments through Claude
offerings for organizational users and platform builders.

The operating model is likely a blend of direct customer engagement and ecosystem-led reach:
- Anthropic establishes product direction, technical standards, and safety expectations.
- Customers require both sound platform configuration and organizational adoption support.
- Product teams benefit when deployment lessons are translated into structured, reusable signals.

This creates a need for an architecture organization that can distinguish strategic exceptions from repeatable patterns. The strongest operating model will avoid treating each partner request as custom consulting while remaining responsive
to high-value customer opportunities.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s public positioning makes trust a commercial requirement, not merely a research principle. Enterprise buyers and delivery partners will expect technical guidance that connects model use to governance, administration, security,
and operational accountability.

Claude’s potential uses span analysis, writing, coding, and complex problem solving. Broad applicability expands demand, but it also increases the risk of scattered experimentation. A disciplined ecosystem motion should help partners
identify use cases where value, implementation readiness, and durable adoption are clear.

The important pressure point is the handoff between platform provider and delivery partner. Anthropic must provide enough structure for partners to produce quality outcomes independently while retaining a clear escalation route for novel,
high-impact, or technically sensitive situations.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
This role likely works across groups with different definitions of success:
- Partnerships seeks committed, productive relationships and scalable routes to market.
- Sales seeks technical confidence, fast deal progression, and credible customer outcomes.
- Partners seek clarity on where Anthropic expertise ends and where their delivery ownership begins.

Influence will come from durable operating mechanisms rather than one-off alignment. Shared account planning, qualification standards, reusable technical assets, escalation criteria, and structured feedback channels can give stakeholders
a common way to make decisions.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic describes Claude as an assistant designed around safety, accuracy, and security. For enterprise adoption, that suggests architecture discussions should include more than model behavior or prompt design. They should address
identity, access, administration, integration choices, evaluation practices, user enablement, and ongoing operational ownership.

Public enterprise materials also emphasize that implementation includes organizational change, not just configuration. This is significant for partners: delivery teams need methods that connect technical launch decisions with adoption
planning, internal sponsorship, user education, and measurement of realized value.

A useful architecture feedback system should classify field observations into three categories:
- Broad product limitations or missing capabilities that affect many customers.
- Reusable implementation patterns that should become partner-facing guidance.
- Account-specific work that should remain within the customer and partner delivery plan.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly describes a network of cloud, technology, and services partners. The implication is a multi-party customer journey in which platform expertise, commercial ownership, implementation work, and ongoing customer support may
be distributed across several organizations.

A public relationship with Accenture signals that the ecosystem can support enterprise deployment and business transformation, rather than functioning as a simple referral channel. The strategic question is whether these relationships can
produce repeatable delivery capacity across accounts, industries, and technical environments.

A strong partner architecture motion would:
- Establish qualification signals for customer readiness, delivery scope, and escalation needs.
- Create enablement paths that build partner confidence beyond introductory demonstrations.
- Support joint customer conversations where architecture decisions materially affect value or risk.
- Convert recurring delivery lessons into better assets, product input, and ecosystem standards.

The most meaningful ecosystem outcome is partner independence with appropriate guardrails: external teams should be able to guide customers effectively while knowing when Anthropic involvement is necessary.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public enterprise surface includes business offerings, deployment guidance, adoption-oriented resources, and a dedicated partner network. Together, these signals suggest a business moving beyond isolated experimentation
toward more formalized organizational use.

That maturity raises the cost of inconsistent partner experiences. As more delivery organizations bring Claude into customer environments, uneven technical advice can create delayed launches, unclear accountability, fragmented customer
expectations, and low-quality feedback for internal teams.

Enterprise AI competition will increasingly depend on implementation credibility as well as model capability. Anthropic’s position will be strengthened when partners can translate the company’s reliability and safety principles into
clear customer practices.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Built technical partner programs across cloud, services, and technology ecosystems.
- Turned advanced AI capabilities into governed enterprise implementation patterns.
- Created repeatable architecture guidance, technical playbooks, and escalation methods.
- Led teams that combine customer-facing technical depth with partner enablement discipline.
- Connected partner, sales, product, and engineering stakeholders around adoption outcomes.
- Improved field-to-product feedback by separating systemic needs from local delivery requests.
- Supported high-stakes customer architecture discussions in partner-influenced opportunities.
- Treated administration, rollout, and user adoption as integral to solution quality.
- Balanced growth objectives with security, reliability, and responsible-use expectations.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Enterprise rollout appears to require both sound implementation and deliberate organizational adoption.

## Do Not Use As Proof
The JD and this briefing are targeting inputs only. Candidate claims, achievements, metrics, leadership scope, technical depth, and partnership outcomes must come from the governed resume/proof graph.

Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 OTE | Reports to Partnerships (partner-facing applied AI architecture) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s enterprise opportunity depends on making advanced AI practical for organizations while maintaining a strong reliability and safety posture. In this context, partner architecture is a scaling function: it converts platform
capability into customer-ready delivery methods that external teams can apply consistently.

The central challenge is not simply growing partner activity. It is creating enough technical consistency that customers receive credible guidance across clouds, consultancies, technology firms, and industry contexts, without slowing the
pace of commercial expansion or forcing every deployment through a central team.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic presents itself as an AI research and safety company building systems intended to be reliable, interpretable, and steerable. Its commercial footprint brings that mission into business and developer environments through Claude
offerings for organizational users and platform builders.

The operating model is likely a blend of direct customer engagement and ecosystem-led reach:
- Anthropic establishes product direction, technical standards, and safety expectations.
- Customers require both sound platform configuration and organizational adoption support.
- Product teams benefit when deployment lessons are translated into structured, reusable signals.

This creates a need for an architecture organization that can distinguish strategic exceptions from repeatable patterns. The strongest operating model will avoid treating each partner request as custom consulting while remaining responsive
to high-value customer opportunities.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Anthropic’s public positioning makes trust a commercial requirement, not merely a research principle. Enterprise buyers and delivery partners will expect technical guidance that connects model use to governance, administration, security,
and operational accountability.

Claude’s potential uses span analysis, writing, coding, and complex problem solving. Broad applicability expands demand, but it also increases the risk of scattered experimentation. A disciplined ecosystem motion should help partners
identify use cases where value, implementation readiness, and durable adoption are clear.

The important pressure point is the handoff between platform provider and delivery partner. Anthropic must provide enough structure for partners to produce quality outcomes independently while retaining a clear escalation route for novel,
high-impact, or technically sensitive situations.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
This role likely works across groups with different definitions of success:
- Partnerships seeks committed, productive relationships and scalable routes to market.
- Sales seeks technical confidence, fast deal progression, and credible customer outcomes.
- Partners seek clarity on where Anthropic expertise ends and where their delivery ownership begins.

Influence will come from durable operating mechanisms rather than one-off alignment. Shared account planning, qualification standards, reusable technical assets, escalation criteria, and structured feedback channels can give stakeholders
a common way to make decisions.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic describes Claude as an assistant designed around safety, accuracy, and security. For enterprise adoption, that suggests architecture discussions should include more than model behavior or prompt design. They should address
identity, access, administration, integration choices, evaluation practices, user enablement, and ongoing operational ownership.

Public enterprise materials also emphasize that implementation includes organizational change, not just configuration. This is significant for partners: delivery teams need methods that connect technical launch decisions with adoption
planning, internal sponsorship, user education, and measurement of realized value.

A useful architecture feedback system should classify field observations into three categories:
- Broad product limitations or missing capabilities that affect many customers.
- Reusable implementation patterns that should become partner-facing guidance.
- Account-specific work that should remain within the customer and partner delivery plan.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly describes a network of cloud, technology, and services partners. The implication is a multi-party customer journey in which platform expertise, commercial ownership, implementation work, and ongoing customer support may
be distributed across several organizations.

A public relationship with Accenture signals that the ecosystem can support enterprise deployment and business transformation, rather than functioning as a simple referral channel. The strategic question is whether these relationships can
produce repeatable delivery capacity across accounts, industries, and technical environments.

A strong partner architecture motion would:
- Establish qualification signals for customer readiness, delivery scope, and escalation needs.
- Create enablement paths that build partner confidence beyond introductory demonstrations.
- Support joint customer conversations where architecture decisions materially affect value or risk.
- Convert recurring delivery lessons into better assets, product input, and ecosystem standards.

The most meaningful ecosystem outcome is partner independence with appropriate guardrails: external teams should be able to guide customers effectively while knowing when Anthropic involvement is necessary.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public enterprise surface includes business offerings, deployment guidance, adoption-oriented resources, and a dedicated partner network. Together, these signals suggest a business moving beyond isolated experimentation
toward more formalized organizational use.

That maturity raises the cost of inconsistent partner experiences. As more delivery organizations bring Claude into customer environments, uneven technical advice can create delayed launches, unclear accountability, fragmented customer
expectations, and low-quality feedback for internal teams.

Enterprise AI competition will increasingly depend on implementation credibility as well as model capability. Anthropic’s position will be strengthened when partners can translate the company’s reliability and safety principles into
clear customer practices.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Built technical partner programs across cloud, services, and technology ecosystems.
- Turned advanced AI capabilities into governed enterprise implementation patterns.
- Created repeatable architecture guidance, technical playbooks, and escalation methods.
- Led teams that combine customer-facing technical depth with partner enablement discipline.
- Connected partner, sales, product, and engineering stakeholders around adoption outcomes.
- Improved field-to-product feedback by separating systemic needs from local delivery requests.
- Supported high-stakes customer architecture discussions in partner-influenced opportunities.
- Treated administration, rollout, and user adoption as integral to solution quality.
- Balanced growth objectives with security, reliability, and responsible-use expectations.

San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD
